CONTEXT. The previous page (51r) sets up the one-parameter family f_t(x) = x^7 - 28 x^4 + c(t), with c(t) = 280 - sqrt(t^2+20000) + i t and t real. The constant c(t) runs along the left branch of the hyperbola (Re c - 280)^2 - (Im c)^2 = 20000. That hyperbola has vertices at 280 ± 100*sqrt(2) and foci at 80 and 480. The next page (52) treats the other branch as well: 'Gleichung 1' has constant 280 + sqrt(...) + i t = 477.9898987 + ... i.

At t = 0, f_0 = x^7 - 28x^4 + 138.5786 has three real roots. Page 51r tabulates them: 1.54516, -1.45325, 2.97087. It then follows these three roots as t goes from 0 to 460.6968.

THIS PAGE (51v) follows the remaining four roots, which form two complex-conjugate pairs at t = 0. One root from each pair is followed continuously along the whole path, t from -460.6968 through 0 to +460.6968, at the stations
460.6968 (IV), 400, 300, 241.6609, 200, 138.56406 (III), 100, 27.73434 (II), 0 (I),
then back out through the same |t| values. The page lists only |t|.

SIGN CONVENTION (mine, verified numerically).
- Column 1 starts at t = -460.6968. I checked that 0.93083+1.70514i satisfies z^7 - 28z^4 = 201.915 + 460.697i, so c = -201.915 - 460.697i. It ends at t = +460.6968.
- Column 2 runs the other way: from t = +460.7 down to t = -460.7. Equivalently, its complex conjugate runs from t = -460.7 to t = +460.7.
- Linearizing at t = 0 confirms this. With dz = -i dt / f'(z):
  - Column 1 at 0.04267+1.48473i has dz ≈ dt*(-0.00261+0.00029i). For dt = +27.73 this predicts -0.0723+0.0081i; the table gives -0.0735+0.0069i.
  - Column 2 at -1.57406+2.63397i has dz ≈ dt*(-0.000056-0.000378i). This matches the first-half II entry for dt = +27.73.
- Gauss apparently always writes down the member of a conjugate pair that keeps a positive imaginary part. Page 51r mixes conventions the same way: its columns 2 and 3 are, strictly, roots for -t.

CONTENT. Each entry x satisfies x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 - sqrt(t^2+20000) ± i t ≈ 0 to about 5 decimals.
- At I (t = 0), the pairs 0.04267 ± 1.48473i and -1.57406 ± 2.63397i together with the three real roots sum to 0. This is required, since there is no x^6 term.
- At t = +460.6968 I collected all seven roots: 1.70718+1.08166i and the conjugates of the other two 51r entries; -1.01144+2.18095i; -1.47112+2.22598i; 0.93083-1.70514i; -1.47951-2.79896i. Their sum is 0.00001 + 0.00000i.
- At III (|t| = 138.56406 = 80*sqrt(3), so sqrt(t^2+20000) = 140*sqrt(2) and c = 82.0101013 ± 138.5640646i), the entries reappear as high-precision roots on p.52, 'Gleichung 2':
  - 0.41561+1.45566i is the conjugate of x5;
  - -0.35955+1.54121i is x4;
  - -1.56130+2.57246i is x6;
  - -1.54976+2.68305i is the conjugate of x3.
  So Zug III was computed precisely, and the table is a continuation linking such precise solutions.

THE ZUG STATIONS. At 241.6609 we have t^2 + 20000 = 280^2, so c is purely imaginary there. The meaning of II (27.73434) and IV (460.6968) is not certain. They are presumably points where the path meets the 'Züge' (curves or lines) of a figure.

PURPOSE. This is numerical continuation of all seven roots of a polynomial along a path in the coefficient (c) plane. It tracks how the roots move and pair up, i.e. their monodromy. The critical values of x^7 - 28x^4 + c are c = 0 and c = 192*16^(1/3)*w^k, with w^3 = 1; these are about 483.8 and -241.9 ± 419.0i. The study very likely relates to Gauss's work on the continuity and topology of root paths, connected with his proofs of the fundamental theorem of algebra (1799/1849). That connection is my interpretation.
errors: No numerical errors found. Spot checks give residuals consistent with 5-decimal rounding: col.1 at t=-460.7, col.1 and col.2 at t=0, col.2 at both ends (the col.2 end check is only rough, about 1% residual, consistent with my hand arithmetic). Sums of roots vanish at t=0 and t=460.7.

The sign of t is not stated. Column 1 runs t from -460.7 to +460.7, column 2 from +460.7 to -460.7 (or equivalently its conjugate). The page lists only |t|, so the table is ambiguous without checking. On p.51r, columns 2 and 3 likewise correspond to -t, while the header formula has '+ i.t'.

results.what: Numerical tracking (continuation) of the complex roots of x^7-28x^4+c(t) as c moves along a hyperbola branch, with tabulated root positions at intermediate stations and a cross-check against high-precision solutions at chosen stations.
results.modern_name: Numerical continuation / homotopy root tracking; empirical monodromy of algebraic function roots
results.usually_credited_to: Root continuity and monodromy ideas: Puiseux (1850), Riemann (1851/57). Numerical homotopy continuation: 20th century (Davidenko 1953, Garcia–Zangwill, Morgan, etc.)

results.what: Choice of path stations: t=80*sqrt(3) gives sqrt(t^2+20000)=140*sqrt(2); t=sqrt(58400) gives a purely imaginary constant.
results.modern_name: Parametrization of the path in coefficient space

deep.surprise_reason: The arithmetic is routine for Gauss. What stands out is a carefully computed table following all seven roots of a septic along a closed path in the complex coefficient plane, with precise solutions at key points (p.52). That is an early hands-on study of root continuation and monodromy, presumably tied to his FTA work. Gauss's interest in the continuity of roots is known, so this is a notable but not major unpublished detail.
